name: Artificial Intelligence
description: From the Dartmouth workshop of 1956 to chatbots and image generators: the booms, the winters and the systems that marked each step.

checkpoints.name: The first wave
checkpoints.note: The field gets its name at a summer workshop at Dartmouth College in 1956. Early programs prove theorems, hold simple conversations and steer robots, and researchers predict a thinking machine within a generation.

checkpoints.name: The first AI winter
checkpoints.note: The promises are not kept. By 1974 funders in the United States and Britain have cut their support, and AI research goes quiet.

checkpoints.name: The expert systems boom
checkpoints.note: Programs that hold the rules of a human expert make money for companies. Japan launches its Fifth Generation project in 1982 and other countries hurry to answer it.

checkpoints.name: The second AI winter
checkpoints.note: The market for special AI computers collapses in 1987 and expert systems prove costly to keep up. Funding falls away again, and for years researchers avoid even the name AI.

checkpoints.name: Learning from data
checkpoints.note: Programs that learn from large amounts of data take over from hand-written rules. Statistical methods quietly improve search, translation and speech, and in 2011 IBM's Watson wins the quiz show Jeopardy! and Apple's Siri puts a voice assistant on a phone.

checkpoints.name: Deep learning
checkpoints.note: In 2012 a neural network, AlexNet, wins a picture-recognition contest by a wide margin. Networks trained on huge amounts of data go on to beat people at Go, power voice assistants and predict the shapes of proteins.

checkpoints.name: The generative AI boom
checkpoints.note: Image generators and then ChatGPT put AI that writes and draws in front of the public. ChatGPT passes 100 million users within two months of its release in late 2022.
